summary: Kickoff for vendor onboarding focusing on pricing tiers, SLA requirements, DPA redlines and procurement timeline. Customer requested explicit latency SLOs, audit log/access controls, and data residency commitments. Redwood AE/SE clarified hosted vs dedicated options and proposed next steps for redlines, runbook, and technical preflight.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21 14:32 UTC; Duration: ~44m; Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay hey everyone thanks for taking the time really appreciate it. quick agenda — pricing & SLA ask, DPA redline points, security prechecks, and procurement timeline. if we can get those aligned today that's the goal.

[00:24] Anna (Mercury): thanks Maya, yes we have about 40 minutes. i'll jump in with timeline and what we need from legal side, ben will cover procurement flow and tom will do legal specifics. claire has security asks.

[00:41] Ben (Mercury): hey all — procurement is looking to close vendor selection by Apr 8, internal approvers are finance and platform ops. we have a PA review on Apr 1. key for us is predictable cost model and defined SLA for latency and availability.

[01:07] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick clarification — when you say latency SLA are you expecting P50/P95/P99 numbers per route or a single apdex style SLA? also are we talking per-request or aggregated over a month?

[01:32] Claire (Mercury): we want P95 and P99 for the main text generation endpoints, P99 ideally under 300ms for simple prompts but we can be flexible if dedicated capacity is required. also KV cache performance matters since we do long chat histories.

[02:05] Sana (Redwood CSM): noted — i'll capture those as requirement bullets.

[02:20] Tom (Mercury Legal): on the DPA: our privacy team flagged data retention clauses around logs and model outputs. we need a clear retention cap for logs used in observability and a KMS/KV separation if customer-managed keys are required.

[02:48] Maya: perfect, this is all great. i'll call out three paths: hosted (fastest onboarding, usage pricing), dedicated pools (reserved capacity, can hit the P99 targets reliably), and private (VPC/on-prem for full control). each has different SLA and pricing tradeoffs.

[03:20] Anna: cost predictability is top of mind — hosted variable billing is ok but we need soft caps and burst controls. procurement will need a burn-rate demo or forecast.

[03:44] Ethan: we have a cost projection template — we can map expected tokens per month to cost buckets and show where dedicated makes sense. i'll attach a sample sheet. also on caching: prefix/KV caching can reduce token spend significantly for conversation workloads.

[04:10] Ben: one blocker is our data residency requirement for EU customers — can you confirm region availability and egress controls?

[04:32] Maya: yes we support region pins in the hosted panel and Dedicated can be provisioned in eu-west1 with Audit logs. for Private we can do a VPC with egress restrictions. we'll share the region map and egress policy doc: https://redwood.example.com/regions-and-egress (note: link is placeholder in the transcript).

[05:05] Claire: on compliance — do you have SOC2 + ISO? Also are audit logs tamper-evident and accessible for our SOC reports?

[05:24] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we can provide the cert pack under NDA. audit logs are stored and can be exported; tamper-evidence is via signed logs and retention policies, we can surface log export to your SIEM or through S3 with restricted role.

[06:01] Tom: about the DPA redlines: main asks are stricter data deletion timelines, specific subprocessor list requirement, and a clause around model training/derivative uses — we need assurance your platform does not use our content to train public models.

[06:28] Maya: short answer: we do not use customer prompt/response content to train public models. for enterprise contracts we can add explicit language. i'll follow-up with the standard wording and any exceptions.

[06:50] Anna: good. procurement will still ask for indemnity caps and SLA credits. typical ask is service credits for downtime or missed SLOs; how do you normally structure that?

[07:14] Ethan: our standard SLA tiers include uptime % and credits on a sliding scale; for latency SLOs we typically propose a reporting and remediation workflow rather than immediate credits, since latency often varies by model/sequence length. but for dedicated customers we can do stronger P99 commitments and associated credits.

[07:50] Ben: okay what does that look like numerically — can you give a sample?

[08:05] Ethan: example: Hosted SLA — 99.5% uptime monthly with 10% service credit for missing target. Dedicated SLA — 99.9% uptime and defined P99 latency ranges for listed model tiers; credit scale increases for repeated misses. i'll email the sample SLA matrix.

[08:38] Claire: security question — do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for encrypting at rest? and how is key rotation handled?

[08:55] Maya: yes CMK via KMS is supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can opt-in to managed KMS or an enterprise-managed key with additional contract. rotation: we support scheduled rotation and key rollover with a vault-based approach, plus HSM-backed KMS integrations.

[09:22] Anna: do you provide attestations or logs that show key usage by tenant?

[09:30] Ethan: yes we provide KMS audit logs with key use events; we can export to your SIEM. there is some latency in log availability (usually seconds to minutes).

[09:55] Maya: returning to procurement timeline — Ben you said Apr 8 target for vendor selection. do you expect procurement to require a signed MSA before then or is a term sheet enough to get to PO stage?

[10:12] Ben: ideally we want MSA signed by Apr 8. we can do a term sheet to lock pricing but legal wants the DPA and MSA language agreed to avoid surprises.

[10:30] Tom: on redlines — we will likely push on liability caps and the model-training clause. also we need stronger audit rights for certain regulated data subsets.

[10:49] Maya: understood. i'll propose two MSA variants: standard and enterprise (with expanded audit/KMS controls). we'll mark the enterprise as the path for Private/Dedicated.

[11:12] Anna: great. on pricing — we need a clear path from POC pricing to production pricing and any volume discounts. one-off fees for Dedicated setup should be spelled out.

[11:30] Ethan: yes, Dedicated typically has a one-time provisioning/setup fee plus monthly reserved capacity. we can show three pricing scenarios (POC, mid-scale, production) and the break-even when dedicated becomes cheaper.

[12:00] Maya: for the procurement deck i'll include: a one-page pricing summary, SLA snapshot, DPA highlights, and the security pack link. is that acceptable?

[12:14] Anna: yes please. also include an appendix with the model catalog and CPU/GPU footprints for each model tier. procurement will want that for cost modelling.

[12:30] Ethan: will do. i'll attach a model footprint table and a small runbook that shows expected P99 by sequence length on standard GPU configs.

[12:55] Ben: one additional question — do you have rate limits and quota enforcement configurable per token route? We need per-service quotas to prevent runaway costs.

[13:12] Ethan: yes per-route quotas, hard and soft limits, and token budgets per key. We can set burst windows, throttles, and automated alerts to owners.

[13:35] Claire: regarding logs and model outputs — we need to know exactly which logs include prompt text, response text, and whether those are retained by default.

[13:50] Maya: default hosted logs keep prompts & responses for 30 days for debugging, but for enterprise we can reduce retention or disable storing PII. we'll capture that as a DPA clause and provide the controls UI screenshot in the follow-up.

[14:20] Speaker 1 (auto): [crosstalk].

[14:40] Tom: can you confirm your subprocessors list and whether any model inferencing happens in third-party clouds outside the region?

[14:58] Maya: subprocessors list is in our vendor pack. model inference runs in the region you select; for hosted there are some managed services for queuing/monitoring that may be globally replicated for resilience but we can mark them as non-customer-data-processing where appropriate.

[15:30] Anna: sounds good. procurement asks for a standard escrow path or fallback plan if you deprecate a core model. what's Redwood's approach there?

[15:50] Ethan: for model deprecation we provide version pinning and a deprecation window with compatibility patches; for enterprise contracts we can add a code/data escrow for critical model artifacts or a transition assistance clause.

[16:12] Ben: about billing — can invoices be monthly in arrears and do you support PO-based billing?

[16:26] Maya: yes monthly invoicing in arrears is standard; PO-based billing supported for enterprise accounts. we'll provide billing terms in the commercial schedule.

[16:45] Anna: ok if we get the DPA redline and pricing grid by Mar 24/25 we can route to legal and finance and stay on target for Apr 8.

[17:00] Maya: that's our target. action items summarized: DPA redline (Maya), Performance/runbook + pricing scenarios (Ethan), customer approver list (Ben).

[17:20] Sana: small note — i'll open a shared drive folder and drop the follow-up artifacts: pricing sheet, SLA matrix, security certs. link will be shared via email.

[17:35] Claire: there is one technical deep-dive we may need: long-context chat with embeddings plus on-device index — can we schedule a 60m session with infra and data team?

[17:50] Ethan: yes we should schedule that. week of Mar 29 looks good for us. we'll scope the session in the follow-up.

[18:05] Tom: legal also wants an explicit clause around deletion: when a deletion request is issued, what's the time to remove logs from backups and caches?

[18:22] Maya: typical timeline is 30 days for backup pruning, we can accelerate documentation for a 14-day SLA in enterprise MSA if required. will mark as DPA redline.

[18:40] Anna: fine. last thing — any competitors we should be aware of in your references? we've seen Anthropic and OpenAI in other RFPs.

[18:52] Maya: yes customers often evaluate Anthropic, OpenAI, and some on-prem inference vendors. our differentiator is the unified runtime and cost-tools.

[19:10] Ben: that covers our questions. recap and next steps please.

[19:20] Maya: recap: Redwood to send DPA redline summary and standard enterprise wording (Maya) by Mar 24; Ethan to send pricing scenarios, performance runbook and SLA matrix by Mar 25; Ben to confirm approvers and target PO date by Mar 26; schedule technical deep-dive week of Mar 29. we will also include security pack and region/egress doc links.

[20:00] Anna: thanks everyone. we'll wait for the doc pack and then route through legal.

[20:15] Maya: thanks, talk soon.

[20:25] End meeting.
